question_text: Was Gatwick Airport's drop-off payment system hacked?
answer_text: Yes, by Gatwick's own account. It says the firm running its drop-off zones had unauthorised access to AutoPay, which charges drivers automatically. Customer details were reached, and a few partial card details. Flights were not affected.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Were Gatwick AutoPay customers' full card details taken?
answer_text: Not according to Gatwick. Its email says that in some isolated cases the card brand, the last four digits and the expiry date were reached, along with payment records. No source says full card numbers were taken.
label: Confirmed

question_text: How many Gatwick AutoPay customers were affected?
what_would_settle_it: Gatwick, Times24 or the Information Commissioner's Office giving a number.

question_text: When did the unauthorised access to AutoPay happen?
what_would_settle_it: Gatwick or Times24 saying when the access began and when it was found.

question_text: Who was behind the Gatwick AutoPay breach?
what_would_settle_it: Gatwick, Times24, the police or a credible report with its own sources naming who got in, or a group's claim reported by credible outlets.

question_text: Which organisations use AutoPay, and were they affected?
answer_text: No organisation other than Gatwick has said publicly that it was affected. Times24, which used AutoPay at Gatwick, runs car parks at airports, hospitals, universities and shops, more than 200 in the UK per The Register.
label: Reported
what_would_settle_it: Times24, ParkPark or another organisation saying which car parks use AutoPay and whether their customers were affected.

question_text: When will Gatwick's AutoPay drop-off payment come back?
what_would_settle_it: Gatwick or Times24 saying AutoPay has been switched back on.
